elevation_datum: metres above mean sea level (EGM96/local orthometric as published)

peaks.name: Mount Everest
peaks.notes: Elevation from the 2020 joint China-Nepal survey (snow height).

peaks.name: Kangchenjunga
peaks.notes: First ascensionists stopped a few metres short of the summit at the request of the Chogyal of Sikkim.

peaks.name: Lhotse
peaks.notes: Normal route shares the South Col route up to the Lhotse Face (C3).

peaks.name: Nanga Parbat
peaks.notes: Western anchor of the Himalaya; climate profile borrowed from the Karakoram.

peaks.name: Broad Peak
peaks.notes: Main summit 8051 m; the fore-summit (~8030 m) is a frequent false finish.

peaks.name: Shishapangma
peaks.notes: Central summit (~8008 m) is often mistaken for the main summit.

peaks.name: Aconcagua
peaks.notes: Elevation per 2012 survey (6960.8 m); 6962 m also cited.

peaks.name: Denali
peaks.notes: Elevation per 2015 USGS/NGS survey (6190.5 m, 20,310 ft).

peaks.name: Kilimanjaro (Uhuru Peak)
peaks.notes: Yohani Lauwo's participation as guide is recorded in Tanzanian sources.

peaks.name: Mount Elbrus
peaks.notes: West summit. East summit (5621 m) first climbed 1829 by Khillar Khachirov.

peaks.name: Mount Vinson
peaks.notes: Elevation from the 2004/2007 GPS surveys. Further members of the Nicholas Clinch expedition summited the next day.

peaks.name: Puncak Jaya (Carstensz Pyramid)
peaks.notes: Access restricted (permits, mine area).

peaks.name: Mont Blanc
peaks.notes: Summit is a snow dome; height varies by survey. 4805.59 m per the 2023 Haute-Savoie survey (4807.81 m in 2007).

peaks.name: Island Peak
peaks.notes: Elevation quoted 6160-6189 m; 6165 m used here. First-ascent party also included seven Sherpas.

peaks.name: Mera Peak
peaks.notes: Mera North 6476 m is the highest point; most parties stop at Mera Central (6461 m).

peaks.name: Lobuche East
peaks.notes: True summit is a short corniced traverse beyond the false summit (~6090 m) where many parties turn.

peaks.name: Changtse
peaks.notes: Rises directly north of the North Col of Everest.

peaks.name: Chamlang
peaks.notes: First ascent by a Hokkaido University expedition.

peaks.name: Thamserku
peaks.notes: First ascent by a New Zealand party (1964).

peaks.name: Taboche
peaks.notes: Elevation quoted 6367-6542 m depending on source.

peaks.name: Kala Patthar
peaks.notes: Trekking viewpoint above Gorak Shep; GPS readings suggest ~5550 m but 5644 m is the conventional figure.

peaks.name: Machapuchare
peaks.notes: Closed to climbing (sacred to Shiva). In 1957 Wilfrid Noyce and David Cox stopped ~150 m below the summit.

peaks.name: Gangkhar Puensum
peaks.notes: Highest unclimbed mountain in the world; Bhutan has banned climbing above 6000 m since 2003. Climate borrowed from the Khumbu profile.

peaks.name: Nanda Devi
peaks.notes: Inner Sanctuary closed to expeditions since 1983.

peaks.name: Meru Central (Shark's Fin)
peaks.notes: Meru North (6660 m) is the massif's highest point; Meru Central via the Shark's Fin is the famous line.

peaks.name: Masherbrum
peaks.notes: Nick Clinch and Jawed Akhter summited two days later.

peaks.name: Chogolisa
peaks.notes: Hermann Buhl died here in 1957 when a cornice collapsed.

peaks.name: Spantik
peaks.notes: First ascent by a German expedition led by Karl Kramer.

peaks.name: Muztagh Tower
peaks.notes: John Hartog and Tom Patey summited the following day.

peaks.name: Trango Tower (Nameless Tower)
peaks.notes: Great Trango Tower (6286 m) is the group's highest point (FA 1977, Rowell, Roskelley, Schmitz, Hennek).

peaks.name: Laila Peak (Hushe)
peaks.notes: Spear-shaped peak above the Gondogoro Glacier; first-ascent record unclear.

peaks.name: Tirich Mir
peaks.notes: Climate borrowed from the Karakoram profile.

peaks.name: Jengish Chokusu (Pik Pobeda)
peaks.notes: A 1938 ascent by Leonid Gutman's party is disputed; 1956 is the generally accepted first ascent.

peaks.name: Khan Tengri
peaks.notes: Rock summit 6995 m; 7010 m including the ice cap.

peaks.name: Matterhorn
peaks.notes: Swisstopo 4477.5 m.

peaks.name: Finsteraarhorn
peaks.notes: Highest of the Bernese Alps.

peaks.name: Dufourspitze
peaks.notes: Highest summit of Switzerland.

peaks.name: Liskamm
peaks.notes: East summit. Notorious for cornices ('Menschenfresser').

peaks.name: Breithorn
peaks.notes: Easiest Zermatt 4000er, from the Klein Matterhorn lift (3883 m).

peaks.name: Dom
peaks.notes: Highest mountain entirely within Switzerland.

peaks.name: Dent du Géant
peaks.notes: Normal route has fixed ropes on the final slabs.

peaks.name: Mont Blanc du Tacul
peaks.notes: First step of the Trois Monts route from the Aiguille du Midi.

peaks.name: Aiguille du Midi
peaks.notes: Cable car top station (3777 m terrace, 3842 m summit) from Chamonix; start of the Vallée Blanche and Trois Monts.

peaks.name: Barre des Écrins
peaks.notes: Southernmost 4000er of the Alps.

peaks.name: Piz Bernina
peaks.notes: Easternmost 4000er of the Alps. Climate profile approximate (Western Alps).

peaks.name: Grossglockner
peaks.notes: Highest summit of Austria. Climate profile approximate (Western Alps).

peaks.name: Zugspitze
peaks.notes: Highest summit of Germany. Climate profile approximate (Western Alps).

peaks.name: Ojos del Salado
peaks.notes: Highest volcano on Earth.

peaks.name: Huascarán Sur
peaks.notes: Highest summit in Peru and the tropics.

peaks.name: Alpamayo
peaks.notes: A 1951 Franco-Belgian claim reached a sub-summit only.

peaks.name: Nevado Sajama
peaks.notes: Highest summit in Bolivia.

peaks.name: Chimborazo
peaks.notes: Summit is the point farthest from Earth's centre (6384.4 km).

peaks.name: Fitz Roy
peaks.notes: Elevation also cited as 3359 m (recent GPS).

peaks.name: Cerro Torre
peaks.notes: Cesare Maestri's 1959 claim is widely discredited.

peaks.name: Mount Logan
peaks.notes: Highest summit in Canada.

climbers: Luigi Amedeo, Duke of the Abruzzi

peaks.name: Mount Rainier
peaks.notes: Columbia Crest 4392 m (14,411 ft).

peaks.name: Mount Whitney
peaks.notes: Climate profile approximate (interior western North America).

peaks.name: Mount Robson
peaks.notes: Highest summit of the Canadian Rockies.

peaks.name: Pico de Orizaba
peaks.notes: Highest summit of Mexico. 1848 ascent by US soldiers is the earliest documented; earlier ascents are possible.

peaks.name: Popocatépetl
peaks.notes: Closed to climbing because of eruptive activity. The 1519 ascent is a historical claim.

peaks.name: Mount Kenya (Batian)
peaks.notes: Eroded extinct volcano; Batian requires rock climbing (UIAA IV+).

peaks.name: Point Lenana
peaks.notes: Trekking summit of Mount Kenya.

peaks.name: Margherita Peak (Mount Stanley)

climbers: Luigi Amedeo, Duke of the Abruzzi

peaks.notes: Far wetter than Kilimanjaro; the east_africa profile underestimates precipitation.

peaks.name: Aoraki / Mount Cook
peaks.notes: Height reduced from 3764 m after the 1991 summit rockfall; 3724 m per 2014 survey.

peaks.name: Mount Damavand
peaks.notes: Ascended since antiquity; first recorded ascent often attributed to the 10th century.

peaks.name: Ushba
peaks.notes: South summit 4710 m (FA 1903, German-Austrian party); North summit 4694 m (FA 1888, John Garford Cockin and Ulrich Almer).

peaks.name: Mount Fuji
peaks.notes: First ascent is a traditional attribution.
